- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10-15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts peak too early and then plateau or slightly decline, while true outcomes often show sharper, delayed peaks or mean-reversion after spikes.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after high peaks; true outcomes frequently drop sharply after a peak, while model holds or slightly rises.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of late-period corrections (last 5-10 days of 30d window), often missing the true low or overshooting the mean.
- Model exhibits “lagged” behavior — forecasts are smoother and more gradual than true outcomes, which show more volatility and sharper transitions.
- Model tends to overfit recent high values, leading to persistent overestimation even when true values are declining.
- Model does not adjust for mean reversion in the 30d window — it assumes continuation of recent trend, while true outcomes often revert to prior levels or lower mean.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the first 5-10 days, then become overly conservative in the last 10-15 days, missing the true mid-range volatility.
